What is the decimal value of hex 2F?
Why do computers use binary instead of decimal?

points.text: Computers use binary because their hardware consists of transistors that have only two states: on (1) and off (0). This makes binary the natural representation for electronic circuits. Using only two states also makes it reliable and easy to distinguish between values even with electrical noise.

questions.question: Why is hexadecimal used instead of binary when humans read computer data?

points.text: Hexadecimal is used because one hex digit represents exactly 4 binary bits, making it a compact and easy-to-read shorthand for binary. A 16-digit binary number like 1111111111111111 becomes just FFFF in hex. It is much easier for humans to read and less error-prone than long binary strings.

questions.question: What decimal number does the hex digit C represent?
Full-Mark Response Convert the decimal number 156 to binary and to hexadecimal. Show your working for each conversion. [4 marks] <div class="

points.text: Decimal to Binary (divide by 2, record remainders): 156 ÷ 2 = 78 r 0 78 ÷ 2 = 39 r 0 39 ÷ 2 = 19 r 1 19 ÷ 2 = 9 r 1 9 ÷ 2 = 4 r 1 4 ÷ 2 = 2 r 0 2 ÷ 2 = 1 r 0 1 ÷ 2 = 0 r 1 Read remainders bottom-up: 10011100 Decimal to Hexadecimal (divide by 16): 156 ÷ 16 = 9 remainder 12 9 ÷ 16 = 0 remainder 9 12 = C in hex Read remainders bottom-up: 9C So 156₁₀ = 10011100₂ = 9C₁₆
